title: 30th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 36 members present. Members first put questions to the Minister of Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development, Dr. Ali Haidar Ahmed, mostly about the student loan scheme: the late opening of this year's scheme, delays in payments and in replies to students abroad, pilot trainees stuck overseas, and political staffing in the ministry. The rest of this part was the preliminary debate on a government bill (introduced by the Hoarafushi member) to amend the Decentralisation Act so that a vacant local council seat is not refilled by by-election when 548 days or less of the council's term remain. Supporters called it a cost-saving and tidying measure, while MDP members opposed it as weakening local representation. After a 30-minute break during the debate and the sponsor's reply, the Speaker said the vote on accepting the bill would come at the day's voting time; debate on the Civil Aviation Bill had started when this part ends. This part closes the debate on a bill carried over from part 1, then takes two committee reports. MPs debated the tobacco control amendment (which stops anyone born in 2007 or later using tobacco) and the nominees for a vacant Broadcasting Commission seat, with several procedural clashes over whether MPs are free to vote as they wish. At vote time the tobacco bill passed, two other bills were sent to committee, and of four Broadcasting Commission nominees only Moosa Rilwan was approved. The sitting ended with the next one set for Wednesday 14 May 2025 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places, so some exchanges are summarised loosely.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked about staff shortages and the number of political staff in the ministry, and about care workers for people needing special support.
Opposed the bill, saying cost saving is its main stated aim and a cheaper way to hold local elections exists.
In the Civil Aviation Bill debate, said the bill itself was fine but kept returning to election timing and other members' remarks; the Speaker asked him to keep to the bill.
On the tobacco bill, supported the aim but asked how it would be enforced, noting that past laws such as the vape ban have been hard to apply outside Male'.

speakers.name: Dr. Ali Haidar Ahmed
positions: Said the loan scheme opens after policy changes, with a student WhatsApp line and a higher-education management app coming.
Said the ministry prioritises technical fields such as medicine and engineering and offers skills training through free Polytechnic programmes.
Said about MVR 157 million had been spent on student loans from January to April and around 40 percent is being repaid.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked how many students applied to this year's scheme and whether all eligible students will receive loans.
Opposed the bill, saying it fits a pattern of weakening democratic checks and that tax revenue is falling.
Continued on the economy and revenue until the Speaker and a point of order asked him to stay on the bill.
Raised a point of order citing the constitution's provision on a member losing their seat when leaving or being removed by their party, saying it does not apply to a vote.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the amendment, said council sizes on small islands should reflect population, and called for audit bodies to check council spending.
Raised a point of order that a member was not speaking on the bill before the House.
Supported the tobacco bill, saying enforcement would run through Customs at import and the Police, and urged members to read the bill rather than rely on headlines.
Raised a point of order saying a member was giving a false picture that MPs could lose their seats over how they debate or vote.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked what relief students get if they cannot find a job when repayment starts, and whether ministry services will move to WhatsApp or Viber.
In the bill debate, said he saw no real saving from the bill, citing stalled school and hall projects, and urged a change so the law is not amended again.
Called the report thorough but worried about heavy fines and young people born from 2007 becoming offenders, and said education and role-modelling may work better.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked what option exists for students abroad who cannot finish courses because money runs short.
Repeated the question when asked to, noting only a few top-up loans are opened.
In the bill debate, supported the amendment and said it would reduce costs and recurring by-elections.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: As a committee member, said the committee has no power to appoint anyone, that the full Majlis decides by vote, and that media claims a candidate was already picked were irresponsible.
Raised points of order saying the committee's scoring and the floor vote were not being influenced by the President's office, and that votes are cast as each member sees fit.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked why the student loan scheme is announced late each year and what that changes for the application deadline.
Said students get no answers to calls and emails to the ministry and asked when this will be fixed.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked who takes responsibility when the loan scheme opens months late and students miss an intake.
Opposed the bill, said seats could stay vacant for 18 months, and asked for it to be taken out.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked what the ministry is doing to train Maldivians for resort jobs given skills gaps in tourism.
Opposed the bill, noting Addu City wards have one councillor each and a vacancy could leave a ward unrepresented.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked whether students' Bank of Maldives card limits have risen since 2023 and whether the number sent abroad has fallen.
Supported the bill as a fix for a recurring problem and criticised earlier governments' spending and taxes.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Introduced the bill: fewer by-elections, tidier law and lower cost, with no by-election when 548 days or less of the term remain.
Replying, cited New Zealand, Australia, Singapore and Sri Lanka practice and asked for further study in committee.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the bill, saying councils with several members still keep a quorum after one vacancy, and criticised the opposition's stance.
Backed the report, saying the amendment protects health because nobody born from 2007 onward could use tobacco, and that no party should oppose it.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked why scholarships are not targeted at fields the country needs most, such as doctors and teachers.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked why stipend and tuition payments to students abroad are late and whether ministry delays could be a cause, not only student paperwork.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked why pilot trainees abroad get no reply to emails, how many are studying overseas and how much has been paid.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked how many million rufiyaa in student loans have been given and whether repayments are being made on time.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Asked about government policies to train young people in skills, as many school leavers do not go on to higher education.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked whether loans can be made easier to get without pleading, and for the ministry's staff total and political staff number.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill and asked that committee review cover any gaps.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the amendment but said decentralisation also needs fairer sharing of island resources, such as local tourism revenue.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Raised a point of order asking whether a member was speaking on the decentralisation bill or a tax bill.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Presented the temporary committee's report on the Tobacco Control Act amendment, saying it consulted stakeholders and the public and agreed its amendments unanimously among members voting.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the Independent Institutions Committee report: nominees were interviewed after a public notice drew no complaints, and those scoring above the committee threshold were put forward.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Raised a point of order saying no amendment exists that removes an MP's seat over how they vote, and that the claim could mislead the public.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Raised a point of order saying members decide for themselves on the floor and are not bound to follow a committee's report in the vote.

decisions: The Speaker said the vote on accepting the Decentralisation Act amendment bill would be taken at the day's voting time.
The Speaker closed the preliminary debate on the bill after the sponsor replied.
The sitting took a break from 10:30 to 11:01 during the bill debate.
Debate on the carried-over bill ended with no further speakers, and the vote on accepting it was set for voting time.
The Tobacco Control Act (Act 15/2010) amendment bill passed 63 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain.
The bill amending the Decentralisation Act (Act 7/2010) was accepted for consideration 58-9 and sent to the Decentralisation Committee.
The Civil Aviation bill was accepted for consideration 69-0 and sent to the National Development and Heritage Committee.
Broadcasting Commission nominees Zeena Zahir (12-52), Aminath Shiyana (11-55) and Shimla Ahmed (14-54) were not approved.
Moosa Rilwan was approved as a Broadcasting Commission member 70-0.
The next sitting was set for Wednesday 14 May 2025 at 9:00.
